voyage.name: Altes Rathaus & Spielzeugmuseum
voyage.content: This was built in 1474 to replace an even older town hall, and was the city chambers until Neues Rathaus was built in the late 19th century. It was bombed during World War II but rebuilt. It's now mostly a ceremonial hall and events venue, but the tower contains a toy museum.

voyage.name: Neues Rathaus
voyage.content: This was built in phases from 1867 to 1909. It's still a busy city chambers, with access only on business, but you can ride the lift to the observation deck of the tower. For most visitors the ornate neo-Gothic exterior is experience enough. At 11:00, 12:00 and 17:00 the Glockenspiel cranks into life: medieval minstrels parade, knights joust (the knight in Bavarian blue always wins) and Morris dancers pirouette to th

voyage.name: Peterskirche
voyage.content: Munich's first parish church was started in the 12th century, but burned down in the great city fire of 1327. It was rebuilt by 1368 in Gothic style. The 92 m main tower (called Alter Peter) stands between the stumps of two original towers. The interior is basilica plan, with an elaborate gilded high altar, richly decorated side chapels and artwork. Roman Catholic mass is held Tu-Su at 10:00, 17:15 & 18:00. You can c

voyage.name: Frauenkirche
voyage.content: This huge church defines the Munich skyline with its twin onion-domed towers, a shade over 98 m tall - the money ran out for the planned spires. It's the Roman Catholic cathedral, but always known locally as Frauenkirche. It was built from 1469 to 1488 in brick because of a lack of suitable local stone; the towers were only completed in 1525, cleverly anticipating a law of 2004 that no structure within Altstadt may e

voyage.name: Theatinerkirche
voyage.alt: Church of St Cajetan and Adelheid
voyage.content: Roman Catholic church in eye-catching Italianate High Baroque, looking like it belongs in Syracuse. The Theatins were an austere monastic order founded by the 15th century Saint Cajetan, and they built several similar churches. This one was built from 1662 as thanksgiving for the birth of Maximilian II Emanuel, which secured the royal succession. The church was damaged in wartime but restored, and is now in the care

voyage.name: Kunsthalle München der Hypo Kulturstiftung
voyage.content: Modern art museum, no permanent collection but rotating exhibitions. It's funded by HypoVereinsbank.

voyage.name: Residenz
voyage.content: Royal Palace and seat of government of the Wittelsbach dynasty, bombed in wartime but rebuilt. The two principal areas are the Treasury and the Museum (separate admission €9 each). The Treasury (Schatzkammer) has a huge collection of ecclesiastical and secular bling, such as the royal crowns, orb and sceptre. In the Museum, the Antiquarium is the barrel-vaulted banqueting hall. The Papal Rooms accommodated Pius VI on

voyage.name: Deutsches Theatermuseum
voyage.content: This museum about German Theatre remains closed in 2022. Some exhibits are on temporary display elsewhere in the city.

voyage.name: State Chancellery
voyage.content: This fills the east side of Hofgarten, housing the Bavarian Minister (president of the Lande government) and his / her cabinet meetings. The central dome was built in 1879 to house the Royal Bavarian Army Museum. It was bombed out in World War II and only restored in the 1980s. The modern side wings were built 1989-93. In front of the building is a memorial to Munich citizens who died in wartime, and a statue of Duke

voyage.name: Haus der Kunst
voyage.content: Grand exhibition hall completed in 1937 in Nazi - Art Deco style. It doesn't have a permanent collection but mounts ever-changing graphic arts exhibitions.

voyage.name: Bayerisches Nationalmuseum
voyage.content: Huge and fascinating museum of European history from the Middle Ages until early 20th century. There's armour, pottery, furniture, fashions, porcelain, beer mugs, the lot; plus Oct-April a display of nativity scenes. The Bollert medieval art collection is only open Th F 10:00-17:00.

voyage.name: Schack Gallery
voyage.content: An extensive private collection of 19th century Late Romantic art.

voyage.name: Museum Fünf Kontinente
voyage.content: Omitting Europe and Antarctica, the former Museum für Völkerkunde is a global ethnological collection.

voyage.name: Kunstfoyer VKB
voyage.content: Changing art exhibitions provided by the art foundation of Versicherungskammer Bayern.

voyage.name: Alpine Museum
voyage.content: A small museum displaying the history of alpine exploration in the Bavarian Alps. It remains closed in 2022.

voyage.name: Beer and Oktoberfest Museum
voyage.content: History of the festival, in a townhouse of 1340. The "Himmelsleiter" is its characteristic early staircase, a straight flight with no corners.

voyage.name: Valentin-Karlstadt Musäum
voyage.content: Karl Valentin (Valentin Ludwig Fey, 1882-1948) was the Charlie Chaplin of Weimar Germany, appearing alongside a padded-up Liesl Karlstadt (Elisabeth Wellano, 1892-1960). Their typical guise was a pair of factory hands raging against their boss, and this quirky museum celebrates their style, which influenced many such as Brecht. The humour is mostly non-verbal but it will help if your German is good.

voyage.name: Michaelskirche
voyage.content: Grand Renaissance church built for the Jesuits 1583-1599 by Duke Wilhelm V, as a bastion of the Counter-Reformation against those awful Lutherans. The Duke nearly busted the state coffers in buying up the land and funding a construction that townsfolk reckoned was too big to stand. And down fell the tower: "I know, I'll build it bigger". This version survived until bombed in wartime and was restored in the 1950s. The

voyage.name: Münchner Stadtmuseum
voyage.content: Extensive museum, occupying most of a city block; absorbing but signage is only in German. The oldest part of the building is an armory of 1500, the newest is the former Uhlfelder department store (all bombed in wartime, but the collections had been taken to safety), and it's growing still. The permanent exhibitions are "Typically Munich!" (how the city acquired its identity), Migration, National Socialism (the movem

voyage.name: Jewish Museum
voyage.content: Small museum of Jewish life in the city - and death. It adjoins the Ohel Jakov synagogue and the Jewish community centre.

voyage.name: Museum of Urban and Contemporary Art
voyage.content: Street and urban art is ephemeral but the idea of MUCA, opened in 2016, is to bring it into the artistic mainstream. There's a permanent collection and rotating exhibitions.

voyage.name: Asamkirche
voyage.content: This Late Baroque confection was built from 1733 to 1746 as a private chapel by Egid Quirin Asam - he could see the altar from his house next door. His brother, Cosmas Damian Asam, did the frescoes. The church is dedicated to St John Nepomuk (1345-93), a Bohemian monk cast into the river Vltava in Prague at the behest of King Wenceslaus IV. Legend has it that Nepomuk refused to divulge the queen's confessional secret

voyage.name: Kammerspiele
voyage.content: Avant garde theatre, often with surprising modern interpretations of the classics. Some performances are in English, and all have English subtitles.

voyage.name: Bavarian State Opera
voyage.content: Shows ballet and opera performances almost every night.

voyage.name: Residenztheater
voyage.content: This stages a variety of classical and modern plays.

voyage.name: Dallmayr Delikatessenhaus
voyage.content: A legendary delicatessen store with market and bakery. Its eat-in choices are the cafe-bistro, bar-grill, and restaurant.

voyage.name: Oberpollinger
voyage.content: This luxury department store was built in 1905 and became a Munich landmark with its three-gable facade. All the pricey top brands are here, look elsewhere for bargains. There's a 5th floor self-service restaurant, with the rooftop terrace open in the warmer months.

voyage.name: Viktualienmarkt
voyage.content: Large open-air market.

voyage.name: Schrannenhalle
voyage.content: This former granary is an indoor shopping centre with a branch of Eataly.

voyage.name: Konen
voyage.content: Department store with a wide range of designer clothing and accessories, and a bar.

voyage.name: Grano
voyage.content: Good pizza and location, so it can get crowded.

voyage.name: Sasou
voyage.content: This pan-Asian fast food restaurant on the south side of Marienplatz serves excellent Asian noodle soups for an affordable price.

voyage.name: Wildmosers
voyage.content: Claims to be the birthplace of Munich Weißwurst in 1857. Excellent food and friendly staff. Good beer, especially Weißbier, in copious amounts. Come hungry, and you'll leave bloated.

voyage.name: Bratwurst Glöckl
voyage.content: Traditional Bavarian restaurant opposite Frauenkirche. Their specialty is Nürnberger Rostbratwürstl - smaller than a standard sausage, so a serving is six instead of the usual three.

voyage.name: Haxnbauer
voyage.content: This traditional Bavarian restaurant 100 m east of Marienplatz remains closed in 2022.

voyage.name: Schneider Weißes Bräuhaus
voyage.content: Echt Bavarian restaurant run by Schneider Weiße wheat-beer brewery, great food and atmosphere.

voyage.name: Tegernseer Tal
voyage.content: Solid traditional Bavarian food and open late, run by Tegernseer Brewery.

voyage.name: Herrschaftszeiten
voyage.content: Under new management since March 2022, this Bavarian restaurant owned by Paulaner Brewery needs to improve.

voyage.name: Tahdig
voyage.content: Excellent Persian cuisine.

voyage.name: Riva
voyage.content: Italian restaurant / pizzeria

voyage.name: Nage und Sauge
voyage.content: This quirky bar has morphed into a salad cafe, but they're huge portions. Cash only.

voyage.name: Katzlmacher
voyage.content: Among Munich's best Italian restaurants, with accordingly high prices.

voyage.name: Prinz Myshkin
voyage.content: Long-established vegetarian restaurant, bright and spacious, good menu selection.

voyage.name: Ratskeller
voyage.content: This occupies the basement of New Town Hall. Great ambiance and trad Bavarian food.

voyage.name: Andechser am Dom
voyage.content: Small brew-pub serving beer from Andechs Klosterbrauerei, an easy day-trip from the city. Excellent beer and views of the cathedral, decent food.

voyage.name: Hofbräuhaus
voyage.content: Munich's most famous bräuhaus, here since 1644, is touristy but great fun; you may need photo-ID to get in. Schwemme is the 1300-seater ground floor beer hall in the original brewery area. There's oompah music at weekends - listen out for the "oans, zwoa, g'suffa!" song, "one, two, drink up!". Bräustüberl is the stylish restaurant on the first floor. Festsaal on the second floor is a barrel-vaulted events venue. The

voyage.name: Augustiner Stammhaus
voyage.content: Beer hall and restaurant of Augustiner brewery, founded in 1294, great atmosphere, beer and trad food. They have another beerhall on Arnulfstraße, see Munich/Maxvorstadt#Drink).

voyage.name: Viktualienmarkt beer garden
voyage.content: This is the only beer garden in Altstadt, just south of Marienplatz. With 600 seats, it serves beer from all the big Munich breweries Augustiner, Hacker-Pschorr, Hofbräu, Löwenbräu, Paulaner, and Spaten. It can feel touristy.

voyage.name: Goldene Bar
voyage.content: An established old bar and café with a large terrace behind Haus der Kunst. Decor fine, service and drinks so-so.

voyage.name: Havana Club
voyage.content: Since 1985 this place has been serving up excellent cocktails. Friendly helpful staff.

voyage.name: Kilians Irish Pub
voyage.content: Kilians is behind the Frauenkirche and offers the usual Irish beers. Friendly place with good beer and grub, occasionally hosts live music, and it's a popular place among expats, tourists, and Germans alike.

voyage.name: Goldener Reiter
voyage.content: Small and authentically grubby basement bar-club.

voyage.name: P1 Club
voyage.content: Posh nightclub that was once considered a favorite of the high society. Today more lounge than discotheque with a large outdoor terrace. "P1" is shorthand for the address.

voyage.name: Pimpernel
voyage.content: Small nightclub 100 m south of Sendlinger Tor. This venue with red plush and mirrored walls once was a hotspot of Munich's gay scene - a frequent customer was Freddie Mercury who lived nearby. Today it is an afterhours house and techno club open after other clubs have closed.

voyage.name: Motel One München Sendlinger Tor
voyage.content: Simple value place just north of Sendlinger Tor and its station.

voyage.name: Premier Inn Zentrum
voyage.content: Reliable budget chain. They have three others across the city.

voyage.name: Hotel Blauer Bock
voyage.content: Basic clean hotel by Jewish and Stadt museums.

voyage.name: Mercure Hotel München Altstadt
voyage.content: Good value chain hotel, clean and well-run. Mercure have four others across the city.

voyage.name: Unsöld's Factory Hotel
voyage.content: Smart place in a former ice cream factory - so you'd expect it to have a/c, but it doesn't and gets sultry in summer.

voyage.name: Hotel Opera
voyage.content: Delightful small hotel just off Maxmonument.

voyage.name: Hotel Bayerischer Hof
voyage.content: Grand old hotel, attracting big name guests since it opened in 1841. It was bombed in 1944 but rebuilt and extended. It's in a great location and its 337 rooms are spacious and well-appointed. But it gets mixed reviews - most guests have a good stay but too many report poor service, comfort and dining. At these prices it needs to be reliable.

voyage.name: Mandarin Oriental
voyage.content: This gets great reviews from travel publications and more importantly from almost all guests. 73 lavish rooms in neo-Renaissance style, and first class service and dining.

voyage.name: Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten Kempinski
voyage.content: An elegant grand hotel with 150 years of tradition, but a string of poor customer experiences indicate that it doesn't live up to its brand name or price tag.

voyage.name: Hotel Louis
voyage.content: Stylish design hotel with 72 rooms, excellent value for its comfort and location.

voyage.name: Hotel Torbräu
voyage.content: The oldest hotel in town, founded in 1490, it's a traditional, family-run place with 90 rooms. Great value, you're getting an Altstadt location for further-out prices.

voyage.name: Glyptothek
voyage.content: This houses King Ludwig I's huge collection of Greek and Roman sculpture: he was determined to make Munich into a new Athens, if necessary by removing the original Athens piece by piece. The principal sculptures are the Aeginetes, excavated in the 19th century from the temple on the island of Aegina. The building, in neo-classical style of course, was completed in 1830. It was bombed out during the Second World War b

voyage.name: State Collections of Antiques
voyage.content: This began as an exhibition venue but is now effectively an annexe of Glyptothek, housing yet more of Ludwig I's vast collection. The focus here is on "minor arts" and it has huge numbers of Greek and Etruscan vases.

voyage.name: Lenbachhaus
voyage.content: A large Italianate villa completed in 1891, with a striking modern extension of metal tubes, this houses modern and contemporary art. They take up the story in the mid 19th century with Gothic and romantic paintings, moving on to the Expressionists, with a strong showing by the Der Blaue Reiter group which included Kandinsky. And lots more from later, such as Beuys.

voyage.name: Palaeontological Museum
voyage.content: Lots of fossils including Archaeopteryx, Triceratops and Saber-toothed Cat. The museum itself is an interesting building, on three floors but an hour is plenty to see it all.

voyage.name: Alte Pinakothek
voyage.content: Contains hundreds of great European masterworks dating from the 14th to the 18th centuries, including the largest Rubens collection in the world. Café Klenze is its pleasant bakery cafe.

voyage.name: Museum of Egyptian Arts
voyage.content: Museum with classical Egyptian antiquities.

voyage.name: Neue Pinakothek
voyage.content: Wonderful collection including 19th-century big-name European paintings and sculptures. Closed for renovation until 2029.

voyage.name: NS-Dokumentationszentrum
voyage.content: Documenting the deeds of the Nazis in Munich - it's a sort of inverse Yad Vashem, ensuring that the names and acts of the perpetrators are faithfully chronicled for all time. It's text-heavy, with translations, so it's an immersive collection if you're comfortable with that style.

voyage.name: Pinakothek der Moderne
voyage.content: Huge display of 20th and 21st century art and design.

voyage.name: Die Neue Sammlung
voyage.content: Museum of industrial design.

voyage.name: State Mineralogical Collection
voyage.content: A collection of minerals including gemstones and meteorites.

voyage.name: Museum Brandhorst
voyage.content: Opened in 2009, this has a permanent collection of modern and contemporary paintings, sculptures and installations, especially by Andy Warhol and Cy Twombly.

voyage.name: St Boniface's Abbey
voyage.content: This Benedictine abbey was founded in 1835 by King Ludwig I to renew his realm's spiritual life, while in no way impeding his liaison with dancing girls. Bombed during World War II, it was only partially rebuilt. The church holds regular services and the king is buried here, as is his queen Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen.

voyage.name: St Ludwig
voyage.content: This Roman Catholic church is opposite the main building of the University of Munich (LMU Munich). It's in Romanesque style, and features the second-largest altar fresco in the world. No, they didn't sanctify the king, the dedication is to Saint Louis IX of France, patron saint of Bavaria, and "Louis" in German is Ludwig.

voyage.name: St Benno's
voyage.content: This neo-Romanesque church was completed in 1895, one of a trio commissioned for the expanding district of Maxvorstadt. It was bombed in wartime but rebuilt to the original design. Outside, St Benno himself teeters on a column, and the statue of a fish with a key in its mouth recalls his days as 11th century Bishop of Meissen. He kept siding with the wrong king and the wrong pope, and when ousted hurled the cathedral

voyage.name: Astor Film Lounge
voyage.content: Plush repertory cinema within the building of camera manufacturer ARRI.

voyage.name: Cinema Filmtheater
voyage.content: Top choice for anglophones, as it only screens original version English language films.

voyage.name: Circus Krone
voyage.content: This is the winter venue for this spectacular circus troupe. In summer they tour Germany, and other concerts and events are staged here.

voyage.name: Daller Tracht
voyage.content: This large store is the place to get gussied up in traditional Bavarian outfits - they stock men's stuff such as Lederhosn and trad dresses (Dirndl). The range is from economical to top-notch.

voyage.name: Munich Readery
voyage.content: This is the largest English-language book shop in Germany. Mostly second hand but they also stock new titles.

voyage.name: Quittenbaum Art Auctions
voyage.content: If you want some fine art for yourself, or to watch an auction where prices routinely exceed €100,000, then visit this auctioneer.

voyage.name: Second Hand Sports
voyage.content: Large range of second hand sporting goods, especially used bikes, skis and snowboards.

voyage.name: Words' Worth
voyage.content: This store just off Ludwigstraße has a good selection of English fiction and non-fiction titles. Some reckon the Readery (above) is better on price and range.

voyage.name: Alter Simpl
voyage.content: Trad restaurant in the university quarter with a student and arty atmosphere.

voyage.name: Rossini
voyage.content: Decent enough Italian, but it's trading on its hour of fame (as are some of its older clientele) as the setting for Rossini the 1997 film comedy of vanities. This is definitely not to be confused with Rossini the 1942 film musical about the composer.

voyage.name: Atzinger
voyage.content: Trad Bavarian cuisine plus your standard burgers and fries. Atmosphere and prices are aimed at students.

voyage.name: Pommes Boutique
voyage.content: Fast food place with good Belgian fries and burgers.

voyage.name: Schall & Rauch
voyage.content: Small cafe-bar by the university with a surprising selection of food.

voyage.name: Frida
voyage.content: Small restaurant serving snacks, burgers and desserts.

voyage.name: Steinheil
voyage.content: Serving trad food at budget prices for students, and their Schnitzels are huge.

voyage.name: Luise 49
voyage.content: This tiny cafe barely holds ten people. The soups are delicious and the place is popular with students of the nearby TUM, so expect to wait a few minutes in line.

voyage.name: Takumi
voyage.content: This ramen restaurant has moved round the block from its former abode on Heßstraße. It's a tiny place and waits of an hour to get in are common. They go heavy on the miso, shoyu or shio so some customers find meals over-salty.

voyage.name: Il Mulino
voyage.content: Value-for-money Italian, with standard pizza, pasta and fish.

voyage.name: Brasserie Tresznjewski
voyage.content: Trad fare including late breakfasts.

voyage.name: Augustiner-Keller
voyage.content: This brewery was first documented in 1328, within the Augustinian monastery next to Frauenkirche, where they nowadays run a restaurant. The monastery was dissolved in 1803 (no, not in the beer) and the business has mostly been in private ownership since, on various near-centre sites - they've not followed the modern trend of an edge-of-city industrial park. Their beers are popular in south Germany but little is expor

voyage.name: Löwenbräukeller
voyage.content: This brewery was founded in 1383, perhaps on Löwengrube near Frauenkirche - "Löwen" means lions. From 1826 to 1851 production migrated to its present site, with the Bräukeller across the street opened in 1883. The company grew by acquisition and has always exported strongly, with some brewing under license elsewhere, so it's the best-known German brand abroad. The traditional beer garden and beer hall seats 2000 and

voyage.name: Bar Sehnsucht
voyage.content: A bar with a unique interior - motorcycles on the wall, red velvet couches in the corners and bras hanging from the ceiling lights. It fills up fast at weekends, so get here early.

voyage.name: Cafe Kosmos
voyage.content: Lively friendly cafe-bar, popular with those staying in the nearby hostel strip, and it gets very full after dark.

voyage.name: Home Munich
voyage.content: Cozy retro bar decorated with living room and industrial items. Some staff think "cool" means unpleasant.

voyage.name: Moejo 91
voyage.content: Themed on a dockland pub. It's mostly an event venue, booked out to private parties, individual visitors have variable experience.

voyage.name: Salon Irkutsk
voyage.content: The bar is a blend of a live club with an art gallery, with Russian snacks.

voyage.name: Alter Ofen
voyage.content: Pub with a vintage interior and inexpensive food and drink.

voyage.name: Stadion an der Schleißheimer Straße
voyage.content: Lively football pub, mobbed when Bayern Munich or UEFA Champions League games are on.

voyage.name: Rote Sonne
voyage.content: Legendary techno club, many complaints of aggressive bouncers.

voyage.name: Pacha Munich
voyage.content: This fashionable techno and house club is the Munich franchise of the Pacha brand.

voyage.name: Call Me Drella
voyage.content: Arty club with live performances all night long. Dress to impress, age minimum 22. There's a quieter outside area for conversation.

voyage.name: Drunken Monkey
voyage.content: Small and cozy electronic music club decked with hundreds of colorful light bulbs in the basement of Enter The Dragon Vietnamese restaurant.

voyage.name: Lost Weekend
voyage.content: Daytime this is a coffee shop, vegan cafe and bookshop. Around 20:00 it morphs into a live performance venue with jazz, rock, blues and electro.

voyage.name: Minna Thiel
voyage.content: Small canopied beer-garden centred on an old railbus, along with a cargo container and telephone booth, with live music and DJs.

voyage.name: Palais Club
voyage.content: Popular techno club with plushy red charm. Free entry until midnight, and it only starts getting populated then.

voyage.name: Sauna
voyage.content: The clue's in the name: it's hot and steamy, with people packed together. Music is 1980s and 90s.

voyage.name: Tumult
voyage.content: Underground punk club, a rarity in Munich, with clientele to match the music.

voyage.name: The 4You
voyage.content: Clean well-run hostel in good central location. The hostel has its own bar and bike rental.

voyage.name: A&O Hostel München Hackerbrücke
voyage.content: Basic but well-run chain hostel, good value for what you're paying.

voyage.name: Hotel Pension Am Siegestor
voyage.content: Great reviews for comfort and welcome at this B&B next to the Siegestor.

voyage.name: Hotel-Pension Theresia Regina
voyage.content: This remains closed in 2022.

voyage.name: Leonardo Boutique Hotel München
voyage.content: Older hotel near the university, some fittings tatty or broken.

voyage.name: Hotel Antares
voyage.content: Small hotel convenient for the university.

voyage.name: King's Hotel Center
voyage.content: Excellent place by the main railway station, saves you when you're stranded.

voyage.name: ibis Munich City
voyage.content: Reliable Accor chain hotel 150 m north of the main railway station.

voyage.name: Erzgiesserei Europe
voyage.content: This comfy four-star gets good reviews. With underground car park.

voyage.name: Citadines Arnulfpark
voyage.content: Modern, comfortable and reasonably priced aparthotel. Parking is expensive, but that's inevitable this close to the city centre.

voyage.name: King's Hotel First Class
voyage.content: Clean friendly place a short walk to Old Town. Not to be confused with King's Hotel Center 100 m further west.

voyage.name: Charles Hotel
voyage.content: High standards at this Rocco Forte luxury hotel and spa, facing the Old Botanical Garden.

voyage.name: Children's Museum
voyage.hours: School term Thu Fri 14:00-17:00, Sat Sun 10:00-17:00; school holidays Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00
voyage.content: It's perhaps a misnomer, it's more like a crafts & play space, but could save the family sanity one wet day.

voyage.name: Deutsches Museum
voyage.alt: German Museum of Masterpieces of Science and Technology
voyage.content: Enormous museum of science and technology, needing a full day, and even then you need to prioritise which galleries to explore - though half the fun is discovering the secrets of technology you'd never considered. Themes include natural sciences (from atom physics to music), materials and energy (including robotics), transport including aerospace, environment, health, agriculture and food, IT, communications and phot

voyage.name: St Maxmilian Church
voyage.content: In a prominent position on the banks of the Isar, this Roman Catholic parish church was mostly complete by 1908, though the sacristry was only added in 1938. It was bombed during wartime but restored by 1953. It was again closed for restoration during 2021. The mighty organ and church bells will get your attention when they sound off, and the church sometimes hosts concerts. Since 1993 the pastor has been the flamboy

voyage.name: Old South Cemetery
voyage.content: This was established in 1563 when plague overfilled the church graveyards, and bodies needed to be interred beyond city limits. St Stephan's church at its main north entrance was built at the same time. From 1788 to 1868 it was Munich's single collective burial ground, becoming non-denominational, so it's the last resting-place of some 14,000 citizens. The roll-call includes Josef von Fraunhofer, Friedrich von Gärtne

voyage.name: St Paul's church
voyage.content: Massive Roman Catholic church in neo-Gothic style, completed in 1906. It was bombed out in 1944 but rebuilt, albeit with a simpler interior. Its best known feature is the 97 m main tower. In 1960 a Convair C-131 transport plane lost power on take-off, clipped the tower and crashed into the street, killing all 20 on board and 32 in a passing tram. The tower can be climbed to a viewing platform but only during Oktoberf

voyage.name: St Andreas' church
voyage.content: Striking modern Roman Catholic church completed in 1953. Even more striking are the five bells, which are trying their best to be heard in Hamburg.

voyage.name: Bavaria statue and Hall of Fame
voyage.hours: Apr-mid Oct daily 09:00-18:00; in Oktoberfest statue 09:00-20:00, hall closed
voyage.content: Early 19th century Bavaria was a pawn in conflicts between Austria and Napoleonic France, so when Ludwig I came to the throne in 1825, he sought an iconic statue to symbolise Bavaria's strength and independence, and a hall of fame to celebrate its heroes. There was a design competition, and since Ludwig was a great admirer of classical Greece, that was the style that won. The ensemble was completed in 1850, and casti

voyage.name: Verkehrszentrum
voyage.content: This branch of Deutsches Museum is about transport of every kind. The main themes are urban transport, travel, and mobility and technology. The building was the halls of Münchner Messe, the trade fairs, until they moved out to the eastern suburbs.

voyage.name: State Theater at Gärtnerplatz
voyage.content: Opulent theatre-house opened in 1865 and mainly showing opera, with occasional operettas, musicals, and ballets.

voyage.name: Deutsches Theater München
voyage.content: Grand theatre opened in 1896, the style is called neo-baroque but in this upmarket district the building doesn't greatly stand out. Early fare was music hall, popular comedy and light theatre. Nowadays their programme is mostly musicals, with some theatre, ballet and operetta. The theatre was extensively refurbished 2008-2014.

voyage.name: Münchner Volkstheater
voyage.content: The theatre left its old venue on Brienner Straße in 2021 and now dwells down near the southside railway tracks. They offer an eclectic mix, often contemporary takes on the classics.

voyage.name: Galeria
voyage.content: This department store, built in 1904/05, fills the block between the railway station and Karlplatz S- and U-Bahn. It's got everything, and is very busy on Saturdays.

voyage.name: Optimal Records
voyage.content: Shops for vinyl records are everywhere disappearing but Optimal record store, founded in 1982, is still going. These are new records, they don't run an exchange, and they also stock CDs, mags, books and wine. So that's your nostalgic weekend sorted. The stock is mostly techno, house and electro vinyl, and famous names from the vinyl era are occasionally seen here.

voyage.name: Public Possession
voyage.content: Record store dealing in electro, techno, house and disco vinyl and with artistic merchandise.

voyage.name: Bergwolf
voyage.content: German fast-food, dishing up sausages, fries, beer and rock music late into the night. Reviewers continue to praise their Currywurst.

voyage.name: Haguruma
voyage.content: This Japanese restaurant continues to delight.

voyage.name: Bistro Lavash
voyage.content: Reliable Turkish eatery with good menu selection.

voyage.name: Roecklplatz
voyage.content: Traditional German food with modern flair, plus popular but un-touristy beer garden.

voyage.name: Faun
voyage.content: Bistro with affordable Bavarian and international cuisine. There's seating outside and the indoor area has an Art Nouveau ceiling; the sports bar is mobbed during big matches.

voyage.name: Deutsche Eiche
voyage.content: This hotel restaurant caters to non-residents and gets great reviews. Look for the row of flags, including an LGBT flag to mark the hotel's history in the gay community, and usually a platter of raw mushrooms outside the main entrance. Sometimes they display a poisonous mushroom saying that it's for the mother-in-law, that's how inclusive they are.

voyage.name: Fraunhofer
voyage.content: Trad Bavarian restaurant with a theatre and cinema in the backyard: this was film director Fassbinder's favorite restaurant.

voyage.name: München 72
voyage.content: Comfy café-bar with 70s decor in homage to Munich's 1972 Olympics.

voyage.name: Sushi+Soul
voyage.content: Japanese restaurant with a modern atmosphere and freshly prepared sushi and sashimi. They also have a large assortment of cocktails and Japanese whiskeys. Pricey, and some reviewers aren't convinced it's worth the extra.

voyage.name: Münchner Stubn
voyage.content: Trad Bavarian fare, right by the station but doesn't feel tourist-trappy.

voyage.name: Bavariapark beer garden
voyage.content: Beer garden and restaurant serving Augustiner with 1500 seats, on the park between Deutsches Museum Verkehrszentrum and the Bavaria Statue. It's also next to Theresienwiese the venue of Oktoberfest, but if you come out of there in need of a beer something's amiss.

voyage.name: Paulaner Bräuhaus
voyage.content: Beer garden with 800 seats at the site of the original Paulaner brewery. Decent food and slick service, but some street noise from the busy intersection, so you can't imagine you've been hiking in the Bavarian forests.

voyage.name: Alte Utting
voyage.content: This ship was a steamer on a Bavarian lake until 2016. It now perches on a railway bridge, an offbeat venue undecided whether it's The Flying Dutchman or The Flying Scotsman. It has beer, grills, live music, cabaret and disco, a beer garden, and from the upper deck surely the most unusual view over Munich.

voyage.name: Zur Gruam
voyage.content: Once a corner pub, this tiny venue has turned into a trendy bar and afterhours-club with disco feeling and live electro DJs.

voyage.name: Couch Club
voyage.content: Guests sit in comfy couches or at the long bar in this cozy place. They have over 100 varieties of gin. The club remains closed in 2022.

voyage.name: Frau im Mond
voyage.content: This rooftop bar on top of the Deutsches Museum, named after the science fiction silent movie by Fritz Lang from 1928, offers a view to the south over the Isar river and events with live DJs.

voyage.name: Kulturstrand
voyage.content: Perched on the tip of Museum Island, this is a bar with various live events. It compares itself to the urban beach of Paris Plage, it's more like a terrace overlooking the sandbanks as the Isar divides.

voyage.name: Lola
voyage.content: Lively weekend late-night bar, refurbished in 2022. The place downstairs, Mucki & Floyd, is no longer a night club.

voyage.name: Niederlassung
voyage.content: A cozy bar specialising in gin. No food.

voyage.name: Robinson's Bar
voyage.content: They bill themselves as a New York cocktail bar, which won't wash if you know New York, but mostly they get good reviews.

voyage.name: Zephyr Bar
voyage.content: Bland modern exterior, within is a very chic cocktail bar. No table reservations so get there early, and cash only.

voyage.name: Bahnwärter Thiel
voyage.content: Techno club and alternative cultural centre that resides in graffiti-covered pile of ship containers. The inventory of the club includes many curiosities such as discarded subway cars, trams, construction cranes or carriages. The venue also has an outdoor rave area where the DJ resides within the cab of a decommissioned subway car. The operators also run the Alte Utting lake steamer which has somehow ended up on a ra

voyage.name: Blitz Club
voyage.content: Techno club in the former historic congress hall of the Deutsches Museum. One of the main venues for techno in Munich with a regular international DJ lineup. It also offers a series of gay events called Cruise. Note that the club has a strict ban on photography and filming.

voyage.name: Kauz Bar
voyage.content: Live music club in city centre, mostly R&B.

voyage.name: Corleone-Neuland
voyage.content: Tiny art bar turning into an electro club at night.

voyage.name: Legal Club
voyage.content: Techno and house club with a wooden dance floor at Sendlinger Tor.

voyage.name: Milla
voyage.content: You're not drunk (yet), the dance floor really does careen at that angle. Clutch your drink firmly while balancing on worn out couches or wooden chairs in this long narrow music venue.

voyage.name: Strom
voyage.content: Small club and live music venue in the basement of an old business house with a focus on indie rock and post-punk.

voyage.name: Substanz
voyage.content: Temporarily Closed. This club hosts indie bands. house or hip-hop music, and shows TV sport.

voyage.name: Wannda Circus
voyage.content: Venue that consists of several old circus tents and hosts techno club nights, indie rock concerts and wild fashion shows.

voyage.name: CVJM Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Clean hostel with good breakfast and friendly service.

voyage.name: 4You Hostel
voyage.content: Clean friendly convenient place.

voyage.name: Pension am Hauptbahnhof
voyage.content: Right by the station, cleaning erratic.

voyage.name: Hotel Jedermann
voyage.content: Basic but acceptable place southeast of station.

voyage.name: A&O Hostel
voyage.content: Right by the station, cleaning erratic.

voyage.name: Euro Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Friendly lively central place.

voyage.name: Jaeger's
voyage.content: Clean and comfortable lodgings, good place to meet other travellers.

voyage.name: Wombats City Hostel
voyage.content: Buzzing hostel, great central location. They have another in Werksviertel.

voyage.name: Hotel Amba
voyage.content: Basic central place, noise from station and street.

voyage.name: Hotel NH
voyage.content: Good location and service, the decor is chain-bland but you'll be too busy in town to notice.

voyage.name: Creatif Hotel Elephant
voyage.content: Great value for its location right by the station.

voyage.name: Carathotel München
voyage.content: Good mid-price place close to Old Town.

voyage.name: Arthotel ANA Astor
voyage.content: Now part of ANA chain, this is a decent mid-price place.

voyage.name: Courtyard by Marriott Munich City Center
voyage.content: A typical mid-range Courtyard property just south of Hauptbahnhof, good comfort and service.

voyage.name: Hotel Präsident
voyage.content: Good value simple hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Royal
voyage.content: Ugly slab of a building but very central. Mixed reviews for comfort.

voyage.name: Hotel Wallis
voyage.content: Comfy central place, most rooms are small but they also have spacious family rooms.

voyage.name: Mercure München City Center
voyage.content: Above-average comfort for this chain, if you can live with the lurid orange-tiled bathrooms.

voyage.name: Hotel München City Center
voyage.content: Small convenient mid-price place.

voyage.name: Hotel Excelsior
voyage.content: Friendly hotel 200 m east of main railway station.

voyage.name: Eden Hotel Wolff
voyage.content: Welcoming hotel, great location.

voyage.name: Le Meridien Munich
voyage.content: Marriott chain hotel, great location and comfy enough, but only mid-range quality for what you're paying.

voyage.name: Sofitel Munich Bayerpost
voyage.content: This was the main post office, with a grand facade, but the inside is modern and efficient, and it's now part of Accor chain. Some noise and disruption from nearby construction.

voyage.name: Museum Villa Stuck
voyage.content: Franz von Stuck (1863-1928) was a painter and sculptor best known for his renditions of mythological scenes. From 1897 he designed this neo-classical mansion. There's a permanent display of his own works plus changing exhibitions of other artists.

voyage.name: Friedhof Bogenhausen
voyage.content: You need to be influential to earn a plot in this small cemetery. Those that did so include film producer Bernd Eichinger, director Rainer Werner Fassbinder, writer Oskar Maria Graf and writer Erich Kästner. It's by the attractive church of St Georg.

voyage.name: Maximilianeum
voyage.content: This is the grand sort-of Renaissance building closing the vista across the Maximilian Bridge, with the road and tramway dividing around it. It was built in fits and starts from 1857 to 1874, the problem being the steep riverbank site for such a heavy structure. Originally a foundation for gifted students, it was bombed in World War II, and since rebuilding in 1949 has housed the Bavarian parliament. They pay rent to

voyage.name: Haidhauser District Museum
voyage.content: Small display of life in the neighbourhood. Exhibitions have varying hours and prices.

voyage.name: Bavarian Public Observatory Munich
voyage.content: The observatory is open to the public M-F after dark with 2-hour tours - Monday these are in English. Pick a clear night.

voyage.name: Sudetendeutsches Museum
voyage.content: The Sudeten Germans were settled for over 1000 years in Bohemia, making up a quarter of the population. This led to ethnic tensions and was the pretext for Hitler's invasions of the 1930s. Post-war they were expelled to Germany and Austria. This museum in a striking modern building tells their story, with signage also in Czech and English.

voyage.name: Eastern Cemetery
voyage.content: This was laid out from 1817 and is still in use, so it holds a large cast of city notables. These include Duke Ludwig Wilhelm in Bavaria (1831-1920), Bernhard von Guden (1824-1886) doctor to King Ludwig II and found dead with him in unexplained circumstances, Rudolph Moshammer (1940-2005) the celebrity fashion designer strangled by a sex pick-up, and Hjalmar Schacht (1877-1970) the Weimar financier. During the Third

voyage.name: Holy Cross Church
voyage.content: Gothic Revival RC church built 1866 to 1886. It was unharmed by wartime bombing and, sitting atop a hill, its 95-m bell tower is visible from afar.

voyage.name: Boulderwelt München Ost
voyage.content: In this large bouldering hall you can test your climbing skills without a harness on 13 different courses. It also has a competition wall, 3 child courses, a bistro, and an outdoor course with slackline park and beer garden in summer.

voyage.name: Hi-Sky Munich
voyage.content: 80-m Ferris wheel giving you a 30 min ride and panorama of Munich and the Alps.

voyage.name: whiteBOX
voyage.content: Contemporary art gallery hosting changing exhibitions. Some 30 artists have their ateliers here.

voyage.name: Silberfabrik
voyage.content: A screen-printing workshop and creative space which offers silkscreen and t-shirt printing courses.

voyage.name: Müllers'ches Volksbad
voyage.content: Have a swim at this Art Nouveau public indoor pool opened in 1901 - bring your own towel. The sauna is temporarily closed to save heating costs, and the cafe is closed permanently.

voyage.name: Prinzregententheater
voyage.content: This magnificent Art Nouveau theatre, modelled on the Wagner-Festspielhaus in Bayreuth, houses the Bavarian Drama Academy. The focus of the shows is on opera and musical.

voyage.name: Gasteig
voyage.content: This is a large cultural and educational complex overlooking the river - "Gasteig" means a steep climb. It's a modern building completed in 1985 which normally houses the Munich Philharmonic Orchestra, the Richard Strauss Conservatory, the city library and community college, and various festivals. However it's closed 2021-27 for rebuilding, and most functions have re-located to Gasteig HP8 in Sendling district.

voyage.name: Daseinstein
voyage.content: Shopping centre with Media Markt for electronics, Netto and Edeka supermarkets, a pharmacy, miscellaneous shops and eating places.

voyage.name: Kaufring
voyage.content: Large department store with fashion, jewellery, books and household supplies.

voyage.name: M2 Music 2nd Hand
voyage.content: One of Munich's oldest second-hand record stores with a huge selection of vinyl and CDs of all genres. Pricey but good quality.

voyage.name: MJ Guitars
voyage.content: Well-stocked shop for new and second-hand guitar purchase and repair, helpful knowledgeable staff speak good English. It was founded by the lead guitarist of the hard rock band Scorpions, Matthias Jabs.

voyage.name: Monkey Island Records
voyage.content: This small record store and bar offers rock vinyl.

voyage.name: Mono
voyage.content: Longstanding second-hand record store and a place to dig for rare vinyl and CDs from indie to electronic music.

voyage.name: Attentat Griechischer Salat
voyage.content: Modern Greek restaurant serving salads, huge portions.

voyage.name: EscoBar
voyage.content: Lively friendly Tex-Mex restaurant near East station.

voyage.name: Il Padrino
voyage.content: Cosy Italian restaurant, good value fare.

voyage.name: L'Angolo della Pizza
voyage.content: Busy place near the station serving Italian staples.

voyage.name: Nachtkantine
voyage.content: This restaurant, bar and live music venue is in the works canteen of the former Pfanni factory. They serve burgers, pizza and pasta but get poor reviews for quality and service.

voyage.name: Henry hat Hunger
voyage.content: Bright pleasant cafe with mostly vegetarian dishes.

voyage.name: El Perro
voyage.content: Popular restaurant offering warm and cold tapas, paella and other Spanish specialities and wines.

voyage.name: Haidhauser Augustiner
voyage.content: Quality trad Bavarian food and drink.

voyage.name: Il Cigno
voyage.content: Lively Italian, draws a student crowd.

voyage.name: Spezlwirtschaft
voyage.content: Restaurant-bar with trad Bavarian cuisine, but the music is hip-hop.

voyage.name: Le Faubourg
voyage.content: Smart French bistro, mixed reviews on whether it lives up to the price.

voyage.name: Sushi Cent
voyage.content: Excellent for sushi and other Japanese specialities.

voyage.name: Tassilo da Sebastiano
voyage.content: Authentic Italian food and wine at affordable prices.

voyage.name: Wirtshaus in der Au
voyage.content: Great reviews for cuisine and service at this trad restaurant in Au district.

voyage.name: Käfer-Schänke
voyage.content: Consistently glowing reviews for this upscale haute cuisine restaurant.

voyage.name: Vinaiolo
voyage.content: Pricey but excellent trattoria in a former pharmacy. Reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Gabelspiel
voyage.content: Fine French cuisine: go for the wine-pairing.

voyage.name: Café Voilà
voyage.content: Long-standing café, bar and restaurant serving Augustiner beer and generous portions of trad food.

voyage.name: Café im Hinterhof
voyage.content: Hinterhof means courtyard and it's an attractive cafe-bar, with regular piano live music and exhibitions. They offer breakfast / brunch throughout the day and have good cakes.

voyage.name: Café Blá
voyage.content: Just what every metropolis needs, an Icelandic café - Blá means blue.

voyage.name: Café Crönlein
voyage.content: Café-bar in a former public restroom, an odd little stone building that looks more like a park attendant's tool shed. There's more capacity in summer when you can sit outside.

voyage.name: Café Hüller
voyage.content: An easy-going café with a pleasant outdoor area in fine weather.

voyage.name: CCC Container Collective
voyage.content: Container Collective is a ziggurat of shipping containers on Atelierstraße (corner with Friedenstraße) on the southeast flank of Ostbahnhof, the start of Werksviertel. It's billed as an art space but (in true bohemian style) no artistic work actually gets done and you come for the bars. As of 2022, these are Bar of Bel Air (daily 17:00-22:00), Transit Rooftop & Bar, and Kaserne de Janeiro cafe.

voyage.name: Dachgarten auf dem Gasteig
voyage.content: Rooftop bar on top of the cultural center Fat Cat (the former Gasteig) with a great view over the city. On one side you can see the city hall, the Old Peter and the Frauenkirche, on the other side the Werksviertel entertainment district and the mountains. The bar spans two levels on the roof, with timbered wooden walkways running along the upper one - past cozy seating areas, flower beds, bushy plants and herbs.

voyage.name: Johannis Café
voyage.content: When everywhere else has closed and you're still hungry, this café at the foot of St Johannis church is still serving in the small hours. It draws a motley crowd.

voyage.name: Maria Passagne
voyage.content: No sign and just a bell at the door so you won't find it unless you're specifically looking. Within is a small, dimly lit bar serving cocktails and sushi.

voyage.name: MH5 Roof
voyage.content: This rooftop bar on top of the orange Werk 3 building offers regual events with techno and house DJs, as well as a view on a small herd of Valais black-nosed sheep grazing on the roof.

voyage.name: Molly Malone's
voyage.content: Irish pub with nice atmosphere and many expats among the guests. Monday at 21:00 is quiz night. Food is middle-rate, the chips are usually good. Has a big selection of whiskeys and TV sport.

voyage.name: Schwarzer Hahn
voyage.content: This dive bar (its name means "Black Cock") gathers a crowd from Gärtnerplatz. Beer is bottled, nothing on draft, and they only take cash.

voyage.name: Carlito's MINIbar
voyage.content: This remains closed in 2022.

voyage.name: Tap-House
voyage.content: This bar at the edge of Haidhausen district offers 200 craft beers from around the world.

voyage.name: Vivo!
voyage.content: Bar and late-night eating place; they're aiming for raffish.

voyage.name: Charlie
voyage.content: Small techno club with a high-grade dj line-up.

voyage.name: Crown's Club
voyage.content: Aspires to be exclusive, door policy erratic, fun nightspot if you get in.

voyage.name: DNA Club
voyage.content: Techno club in a former industrial location in the Werksviertel district.

voyage.name: Gans Woanders
voyage.content: Cafe, cultural centre and concert venue around a Hansel & Gretel house with a large wooden patio for events - many of these are free.

voyage.name: Jazzclub Unterfahrt
voyage.content: Jazz club in the former cellars of Union Brau. Limited food.

voyage.name: Muffatwerk
voyage.content: Former electricity plant morphed into a club and music hall with café-bistro.

voyage.name: Hofbräukeller beer garden
voyage.content: Restaurant and 1800-seater beer garden serving Höfbräu beer, not at all like the touristy Hofbräuhaus in city centr.

voyage.name: Paulaner am Nockherberg
voyage.content: Attractive 3000-seater beer garden open year-round and serving Paulaner beer. They host a beer festival in March.

voyage.name: Muffatwerk beer garden
voyage.content: This 400-seater beer garden is part of the Muffatwerk complex, see above. The basic beer is Hofbräu, but they also serve a cloudy organic beer from Lammsbräu.

voyage.name: Hotel Christl
voyage.content: Small and cozy hotel, good transport links.

voyage.name: Motel One Munich East Side
voyage.content: Modern and sleek interior with simply decorated rooms. Downstairs is the "One Lounge" with a lobby, breakfast café and bar in one.

voyage.name: Motel One Munich-Haidhausen
voyage.content: Modern hotel at the edge of the Haidhausen district. Downstairs is the living-room style "One Lounge" with lobby, breakfast café and bar in one, and a view onto the street through wall-sized windows.

voyage.name: mk hotel münchen
voyage.content: A simple and inexpensive two-star chain hotel.

voyage.name: Motel One München - Deutsches Museum
voyage.content: Another Motel One, 500 m from Deutsches Museum. Comfy and convenient.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Munich City Centre
voyage.content: IHG chain hotel with small indoor pool (no gym), bar, and restaurant. Good breakfast. Directly connected to the S-Bahn via an underground mall.

voyage.name: Hotel Prinz
voyage.content: Pleasant mid-price place, rooms are small but comfy.

voyage.name: Novotel Munich City
voyage.content: Accor chain hotel with 307 air-conditioned rooms, restaurant and bar with terrace, free spa area with gym, swimming pool, sauna and steam bath, underground parking and a separate conference centre with terrace and 5 modern meeting rooms.

voyage.name: Residence Inn Munich City East
voyage.content: Marriott chain hotel with fitness center, steam room and sauna, and each room has a kitchenette.

voyage.name: Hilton Munich City
voyage.content: Well-placed efficient business hotel.

voyage.name: Courtyard by Marriott Munich City East
voyage.content: Good chain hotel close to public transport.

voyage.name: Sankt-Ursula Kirche
voyage.content: In the late 19th century the population of Schwabing grew rapidly, so they built this Roman Catholic church, consecrated in 1897. It's a neo-Renaissance brick building with campanile, and faces north (not the standard east) because of its position at the end of Friedrichstraße.

voyage.name: Sankt-Sylvester Kirche
voyage.content: This was the original parish church of Schwabing, first documented in 1315, until supplanted by St Ursula's. A neo-baroque "new church" extension was added in 1925.

voyage.name: Nordfriedhof
voyage.content: In mid-19th century the city's only cemetery was the Southern in Ludwigvorstadt. It was getting full so a north cemetery was opened in 1868 in Maxvorstadt - and was obviously too small for the burgeoning city. A further north cemetery was created here in 1884. Among the 34,000 interred are singer-actor "Jopi" Heesters, Ernst Mach who gives his name to a measure of supersonic speed, and Oswald Spengler who predicted t

voyage.name: Chinese Tower
voyage.content: This 25 m high pagoda was constructed with the original park in 1790, and rebuilt after World War II in 1952. It has a beer garden, with a Bavarian oompah band performing at weekends from the second floor. It can feel touristy, and horse-drawn carriage and rickshaw tours through the garden start here - see below for the Kocherlball in summer and the Christmas Market. Until the end of 2022, the tower is scaffolded for

voyage.name: Olympiaturm
voyage.content: This 291 m tower was built in 1968 and looks it: the centrepiece for the 1972 Olympic complex. The revolving restaurant (see below) is at 182 m and the observation deck is at 190 m. Until 2021 it housed a rock and roll museum but this has closed. No reservations for the lift, but advised for the restaurant. There's special midnight opening on New Year's Eve.

voyage.name: Sea Life
voyage.content: Aquarium with over 30 tanks and aquatic life from local river dwellers to sharks and coral reefs.

voyage.name: BMW Museum
voyage.content: Extensive museum displaying the evolution of motoring technology, from the earliest days to future concepts.

voyage.name: Herz Jesu Kirche
voyage.content: This Roman Catholic church was built 1997-2000 after the previous church burned down. It's a large blue glass cube 14 m per side, which contains a wooden interior cube. The church within is spare and minimalistic. The entire glass facade can be opened like a gigantic gate. This only happens on public holidays so don't be lured by their "open door" announcements, which will engulf you in prayer and parish activities.

voyage.name: Botanical Garden
voyage.content: Covering 21 ha, the Garden opened here in 1914 when it outgrew its original site on Karlsplatz. It holds some 19,600 species, with an alpine garden, arboretum, rose garden, and extensive glasshouse collections.

voyage.name: Schloss Nymphenburg
voyage.price: Apr-mid Oct adult €15, conc €13; mid Oct-Mar adult €12, conc €10
voyage.content: What began as a modest 17th century pavilion grew and grew into a vast Baroque palace, bigger than Versailles, which was no accident. You view some 20 ornate rooms: one striking feature is the paintings of the many female friends of King Ludwig I. (See Sligo for one infamous paramour, the lurid Lola Montez.) Some areas are closed in winter, hence the reduced admission: the Royal Chapel, the Porcelain Museum and the M

voyage.name: Museum of Man and Nature
voyage.content: Natural History museum on the north flank of the Schloss but separately managed and ticketed. Signage is only in German.

voyage.name: Schloss Schleißheim
voyage.price: Adult €10, conc €8, under-18 free, cash only
voyage.content: Humonguous complex of three palaces. The Old Palace at the west end was a mansion built up into a palace only to be promptly scrapped and rebuilt by 1623. It was bombed in World War II, rebuilt from 1970, and now houses religious art and an exhibition on the former Prussia now in Poland. The New Palace just east was built 1700-26 for Elector Max Emanuel, a sumptuous Baroque confection packed with art work: Großer Saa

voyage.name: Deutsches Museum Flugwerft Schleißheim
voyage.content: The palace grounds were used as an airfield in wartime, and this is now the aviation branch of Deutsches Museum.

voyage.name: FC Bayern Munich
voyage.content: Die Bayern play soccer in Bundesliga, the top tier. They do well and qualify for European tournaments, and matches sell out. (Buy tickets online, but you have to register, to curb the touts and scalpers.) The Arena (capacity 70-75,000), completed in 2005, is a sight in itself, like an inflatable boat with colour-changing exterior; tours are available. In 2024 it hosted games in the UEFA Euro Finals. The women's team

voyage.name: MTTC Iphitos
voyage.content: This is the principal tennis club in Munich. In mid April they host the Bavarian International (sponsored as BMW Open), played over a week on clay. It ranks in the fourth tier of the ATP tournament schedule.

voyage.name: Surfing on the Eisbach
voyage.content: The Eisbach is an artificial side-channel of the Isar, culverted beneath Altstadt but emerging at the bridge on Prinzregentenstraße, south edge of English Garden. Here it drops over a 1 m weir to form a standing wave, surfable whenever there's a good flow of water. Late winter into early summer is best, as its parent river cascades down from Alpine snows and the "ice stream" earns its name. Surfers queue up on the ba

voyage.name: Wannda Circus
voyage.content: They do put on circus acts, but it's more like a tented event venue hosting live music, theatre, alternative fashion and parties. The field gets muddy after rain.

voyage.name: BoundCon
voyage.content: An event for BDSM fans. Held on a weekend in late May. Numerous live professional bondage shows, as well as custom photo shoots and workshops where you can try bondage yourself (advance registration required). For adults only, naturally.

voyage.name: Galeria Kaufhof
voyage.content: This chain department store has some eight locations across the city, but the one at Rotkreuzplatz is the most useful for the northwest districts. There's a market hall adjacent.

voyage.name: Olympia-Einkaufszentrum
voyage.content: This large shopping complex was built in 1972 for the Olympics and expanded in the 1990s. It has a variety of department stores (including another Galeria Kaufhof), boutiques and food stores. There are parking lots north and south side. In 2016 a mall shooting killed nine people plus the perpetrator.

voyage.name: mira
voyage.content: A three-storey shopping mall in Nordheide district opened in 2008. It's a bright modern structure winning awards for this 'n that, but a third of its 70 stores lie empty.

voyage.name: Nymphenburg Porcelain Manufactory
voyage.content: Offers beautifully handcrafted and very pricey porcelain. The factory was founded in the early 1700s to create porcelain for the Royal family. You can look around for as long as they think you might buy something, otherwise they might tactfully but firmly redirect you to the porcelain museum within the palace.

voyage.name: Shere Punjab
voyage.content: This Indian restaurant gets very mixed reviews.

voyage.name: Garbo by the Sea
voyage.content: Cozy restaurant (which sometimes means cramped) with slick service. Good pizza but the specialty is seafood.

voyage.name: Lemar Restaurant
voyage.content: Delicious Afghan food in a sumptuous interior. Cash only.

voyage.name: Seerose
voyage.content: Great reviews for this cheerful trattoria near the top of the southern English Garden.

voyage.name: Tantris
voyage.content: Pricey restaurant but worth it for top continental cuisine. It will help if you like 1970s decor.

voyage.name: Restaurant 181
voyage.content: Pricey restaurant, the "181" refers to its height within the Olympic Tower, which slowly rotates. Food just about right for the price, snooty service.

voyage.name: Wasserman
voyage.content: Trad fare such as giant burgers, pork roast and Schnitzel.

voyage.name: Taj Mahal
voyage.content: Mostly good reviews for this Indian restaurant.

voyage.name: Maui
voyage.content: Hawaii and fusion cuisine, and it's often packed out.

voyage.name: Scarletti
voyage.content: Trad ice cream parlour with a wide selection, mixed reviews on whether it's worth the higher price.

voyage.name: Ristorante Romans
voyage.content: Smart Italian serving excellent meat and fish with Italian wines.

voyage.name: Schwabinger 7
voyage.content: Authentic dive bar with live music, dark interior and low prices - hence popular among students.

voyage.name: Shamrock
voyage.content: Atmospheric Irish pub, with live music and karaoke, so it's the authentic drouthy experience of Friday night in (say) Wexford, Newtownabbey or Letterkenny.

voyage.name: Wintergarten
voyage.content: Small Augustiner beer garden mostly serving locals, and tourists are rare. It has a small playground with swings, slide and sandpit close enough for you to supervise your kids playing. They sometimes have live trad music. It's next to Elisabethmarkt, see Buy.

voyage.name: Milchhäusl
voyage.content: This snack shop in English Garden offers beer, Bavarian food and bio sandwiches, and in cold weather you can have your snack within an Alpine lift gondola.

voyage.name: Biergarten am Chinesischen Turm
voyage.alt: Beer garden at the Chinese Tower
voyage.content: Famous 7500-seater beer garden next to the Chinese Tower in the south section of Englischer Garten. Good selection of trad food, and Oompah bands play from the pagoda on summer weekends. As it's within walking distance from Altstadt it can feel touristy.

voyage.name: Seehaus
voyage.content: Beer garden with 2500 seats by a small lake in the English Garden. This and the artistic boathouse and other structures were designed by Gabriel von Seidl in the late 19th century. Enjoy a beer and Bavarian fast-food while small boats pootle by.

voyage.name: Hirschau
voyage.content: Beer garden at the south end of Hirschau, the deer park or northern portion of English Garden, with a footpath beneath busy Isarring connecting to the southern portion. With 1700 seats, it's seldom crowded, and not touristy. Music is modern rather than trad.

voyage.name: Aumeister
voyage.content: This is at the very north end of English Garden so tourists are rare. There's a bosky 2500-seater beer garden, and restaurant in one of Prince Regent Luitpold's hunting lodges. It remains closed in 2022.

voyage.name: Freiheitshalle
voyage.content: Events venue in an old red-brick factory where mainly rock and alternative music is played.

voyage.name: Zum Jennerwein
voyage.content: Established in 1962, this is a lively friendly dive-bar and club.

voyage.name: Kesselhaus
voyage.content: Events venue in a former boiler house.

voyage.name: Printhouse
voyage.content: Techno nightclub in a former newspaper printing hall.

voyage.name: Zenith
voyage.content: Events venue in a former railway repair hall.

voyage.name: Deck21
voyage.content: This bar is on the rooftop of Olympiahalle next to the Olympic Stadium. Pleasant views in fine weather, but food and drink are overpriced, service is slow, and the place is not accessible with strollers or wheelchairs.

voyage.name: Olympia-Alm
voyage.content: This is a small beergarden in the park 100 m east of Olympiaberg.

voyage.name: OlyDisco
voyage.content: The club is in the former Olympic village, nowadays student apartments. So it's mostly a student crowd, which keeps prices moderate. It's seen better days.

voyage.name: Happy Corner
voyage.content: A rustic pub just west of Olympic park.

voyage.name: Hofbräu am Oberwiesenfeld
voyage.content: Lively brewhouse southeast of Olympic park.

voyage.name: Hirschgarten
voyage.content: Europe’s biggest beer garden with 8000 seats, with a 500-seater indoor restaurant. They serve beer from two breweries and trad food, though you can bring in your own food. It has a small zoo with deer and wild boars.

voyage.name: Taxisgarten
voyage.content: This small beer garden remains closed in 2022.

voyage.name: Peaches
voyage.content: This lively bar serves cocktails and giant pizzas. Great place to meet and watch people.

voyage.name: Backstage
voyage.content: Live events complex with three venues for shows. The smaller ones are more like club / disco and can go on to 05:00.

voyage.name: Campingplatz Nord-West
voyage.content: Very basic campsite and a schlep to reach, open all year.

voyage.name: The Tent
voyage.content: Tent-based hostel open June-Sept. Good vibe, comfy but unheated, bring your own lock for the lockers.

voyage.name: ibis München Parkstadt Schwabing
voyage.content: Value-for-money budget hotel.

voyage.name: Novotel Suites München Parkstadt Schwabing
voyage.content: Accor budget suites, functional enough.

voyage.name: Motel One München Parkstadt
voyage.content: Small rooms but clean and comfy.

voyage.name: Arthotel ANA
voyage.content: Reliable comfy hotel next to Olympiapark.

voyage.name: Mercure Hotel München-Schwabing
voyage.content: Accor chain hotel, small rooms, near public transport.

voyage.name: Flemings Hotel München-Schwabing
voyage.content: Comfy modern hotel in Schwabing, helpful staff.

voyage.name: Hilton Munich Park
voyage.content: Good business hotel with 3 restaurants, bar and indoor pool with fitness center.

voyage.name: Innside München Parkstadt Schwabing
voyage.content: Melia chain hotel with minimalist modern design.

voyage.name: Munich Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: Chain hotel with spacious clean rooms.

voyage.name: Steigenberger Hotel
voyage.content: Smart chain hotel.

voyage.name: Pullman Munich
voyage.content: Large rooms, comfy enough but cleaning and service erratic.

voyage.name: Rilano Hotel München
voyage.content: Decent enough mid-range place.

voyage.name: Andaz Munich Schwabinger Tor
voyage.content: Great reviews for comfort and service at this Hyatt hotel.

voyage.name: Bavaria Filmstadt
voyage.content: Theme park in working film studios: the standard ticket is a 90-min guided tour of the sets (but only in German) and a 10-min ride in a 4D cinema. Discounts if you come by public transport or on your birthday. The studios were established in 1919 by Peter Ostermayr (1882-1967), who then moved elsewhere to make a score of films in the heimat tradition (set in a romanticized horse-drawn bygone Germany, forerunner to th

voyage.name: MVG Museum
voyage.content: Museum of public transport in Munich housed in a former tram repair and assembly shed. They have 25 historic trams, buses and works vehicles on display, with signage in German and English. Another highlight is a U-Bahn driving simulator.

voyage.name: Cemetery at Perlach Forest
voyage.content: This cemetery was opened in 1931 and has 27,000 marked graves plus a plot for "displaced persons", victims of Nazism. Unlikely bedfellows here are footballer Stephan Beckenbauer (1968–2015), members of the White Rose resistance group executed in 1943, and Polish soldiers of Holy Cross Brigade (Brygady Świętokrzyskiej), a right-wing faction who preferred fighting the Soviet Union and each other instead of the Third Re

voyage.name: TSV 1860 Munich
voyage.content: Sechzig ("Sixty") were founder members of Bundesliga, but now play soccer in 3. Liga the third tier. Their stadium (capacity 15,000) also hosts Bayern Munich second team, under-19s and women. Türkgücü München also played here but went bust in 2022, alleviating the problem of fixture congestion. The most remarkable fixture here, on 10 Sept 1972, was a 0-1 away victory for Greek philosophers over German philosophers, w

voyage.name: Bayern Munich training ground
voyage.content: These pitches host junior teams of Bayern Munich, right down to 8 year olds - so some of them will be star players five or six World Cups from now, imagine. The first team also trains here with a public session at least once a week. They're usually happy to oblige with autographs and selfies.

voyage.name: Cosima wave pool
voyage.content: This is Munich's only wave pool. It also has a large sauna.

voyage.name: Harness Racing
voyage.content: In harness racing, jockeys sit in a two-wheel open cart, and the horse has a trotting gait, the gallop is not permitted. Race meetings are usually on Sunday but this varies, see website.

voyage.name: Munich Racecourse
voyage.content: Also known as Galopprennbahn as horses here gallop in the conventional way. The track has flat-racing May-Nov, concluding with the Grosser Preis von Bayern run over 2.4 km.

voyage.name: Michaelibad
voyage.content: Just north of Michaeligarten beer garden, this has a large outdoor pool in summer and an indoor pool.

voyage.name: Staatliches Hofbräuhaus München
voyage.content: This brewery was founded in 1591, and moved to Riem in 1988. They produce over a dozen beers including an Oktoberfest brew. Tours are only available to groups of 10-30, booked at least 14 days in advance.

voyage.name: pep Neuperlach
voyage.content: The pep is a huge department store with over 80 shops, restaurants, and cafés.

voyage.name: Riem Arcaden
voyage.content: A huge shopping centre next to Messestadt West U-Bahn station, with lots of eating places.

voyage.name: Fausto
voyage.content: Café attached to a coffee roastery in a quiet part of the district.

voyage.name: Antica Trattoria Nuova
voyage.content: Good Italian restaurant with outdoor terrace by the river.

voyage.name: Schneider Bräuhaus
voyage.content: Bavarian restaurant and beer garden run by Schneider Weisse, the wheat-beer brewery. Good traditional fare, somewhat cheaper than their more touristy outlet in Altstadt.

voyage.name: Baumkirchner
voyage.content: German restaurant with good atmosphere and food.

voyage.name: Zar
voyage.content: Restaurant and bar with Bavarian, Asian and international cuisine.

voyage.name: Milchreise
voyage.content: Rice pudding bar offering a large variety of lactose-free puddings.

voyage.name: König Ludwig an der Messe
voyage.content: Trad Bavarian fare in Riem mall, convenient for Messe, indifferent reviews.

voyage.name: Michaeligarten
voyage.content: This 3000-seater beer garden serves Löwenbräu beer and a range of trad fare. You can bring your own food to the beer garden.

voyage.name: Forschungsbrauerei
voyage.content: The name means "Research Brewery" and it was established in 1930 to try different brews and test them on customers. The research ended in 1950 and Hopfenhäcker craft brewery now occupies the space. The beer garden is at the edge of the city conurbation, with Neuer Südfriedhof cemetery north and open fields to the south. It's open year-round and only seats 250, so it's sometimes reserved for private parties.

voyage.name: St Emmeramsmühle
voyage.content: Great reviews for this trad restaurant and 1200-seater beer garden in a former mill at the entrance to Mittlere-Isar Island.

voyage.name: Kugleralm
voyage.content: Trad 2400-seater beer garden in Oberhaching south of Perlacher Forst, serving Spaten beer. In 1922 this was the launchpad of the Radler, half beer half lemonade, a "shandy" in English. The legend goes that they were mobbed by cyclists on a hot summer day. The beer ran low so they eked it out by diluting with lemonade, and claimed this was a special mix for cyclists (Radler) as it was lower on alcohol. Such blends wer

voyage.name: Motel One Munich Campus
voyage.content: Standard budget hotel with good transport to town.

voyage.name: B&B Hotel München-Trudering
voyage.content: Modern budget hotel, some way from centre but near public transport.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Express Munich Messe
voyage.content: Usual good quality HI-Express. Stuck out in an industrial area but convenient car access to eastern parts of Munich.

voyage.name: Leonardo Hotel Munich Arabellapark
voyage.content: Basic rooms, some quite small, reasonable for what you're paying. With covered parking(charged), or there may be a free space on the street.

voyage.name: Hotel Perlach Allee
voyage.content: Standard 3-star hotel, with all necessary amenities.

voyage.name: Novotel München Messe
voyage.content: Decent Accor mid-range place, convenient not only for Messe but for transport to city centre.

voyage.name: Motel One München Messe
voyage.content: Good value chain business hotel.

voyage.name: H4 Hotel München Messe
voyage.content: Acceptable mid-range place at northeast corner of Messe, convenient for highway and trade fairs.

voyage.name: Hotel ERB
voyage.content: Chain hotel convenient for motorists and Messe.

voyage.name: Westin Grand Munich
voyage.content: Marriott chain hotel, great slab of a cereal packet and many rooms need renovation. But it's a good location off Isaring and mostly clean and comfy.

voyage.name: Sheraton München Arabellapark
voyage.content: Marriott intended to demolish this building in 2026 - that's been pushed back, but the place is getting limited investment and maintenance. It's barely adequate for the price.

voyage.name: Hellabrunn Zoo
voyage.content: This is east of the river and district boundary but easier to access from the west bank. The zoo was founded in 1911 to present animals in their habitat, and houses 19,000 animals. An extensive re-building project means that some areas will be closed, check the website for current status. Until April 2023 Jungle World is closed so you can't see the lions, and the bat grotto has permanently closed.

voyage.name: Old St Margaret Church
voyage.content: This is a baroque structure of 1712, still in use. It was built on the site of the Sendling Massacre of 1705, which destroyed its predecessor. St Margaret or Marina supposedly lived near Isparta (now in Turkey) around 300 AD, and suffered fantastical tortures at the hands of the Roman governor and a dragon. Post mortem, she was always giving Joan of Arc good advice. Church indulgences (mitigation of punishments in th

voyage.name: New St Margaret Church
voyage.content: Completed in 1913, this is a baroque / rococo church a block south of the old church.

voyage.name: St Korbinian Church
voyage.content: It is part of the same RC parish as the two St Margarets. It's neo-baroque, completed in 1925, bombed in wartime but rebuilt to the same plan by 1951. Corbinian was a 7th century Frankish hermit and bishop. A bear that ate his pack-mule was instructed to carry his bags for the rest of his pilgrimage to Rome, apparently.

voyage.name: St Achaz
voyage.content: This is neo-baroque, completed in 1927 as a larger version of its predecessor of 1569. Achaz or Achatius could be any one of a dozen early Christian figures who were torn to pieces in a spiritually-inspiring fashion.

voyage.name: Hansastraße
voyage.content: A street that has several striking modern buildings, especially ADAC (the German Automobile Association) at No 19, and Fraunhofer-Haus at No 27 (a research institute named for the fellow who discovered dark lines in the spectrum of sunlight).

voyage.name: Westpark
voyage.content: It was created in 1983 to host an International Garden Expo. It's divided by Garmischer Straße and most sights are in the western part: the Rose Garden, the lake with open-air stage for summer concerts and films, a couple of beer gardens (see Drink), and a few exhibits surviving from those shown at Expo. These are the Chinese walled garden, a Japanese garden, Nepali and Thai pagodas and a Bavarian chalet. The eastern

voyage.name: Waldfriedhof
voyage.content: This is Munich's largest cemetery, opened in 1907, extended in the 1960s and is still in use, with over 60,000 burial plots. As the name "Wald" indicates, it's a woodland cemetery, with memorials and the funeral chapel semi-hidden in the trees rather than dominating a bare lawn. Those here include ace fighter pilot Hans von Ritter (1886-1917), Stepan Bandera (1909-59) whose status as a hero or right-wing terrorist ch

voyage.name: Fürstenried Palace
voyage.content: This was built from 1715 for Elector Maximilian II Emanuel as a hunting lodge and bling-mansion. It's nowadays an RC spiritual centre, so other visitors can only admire the exterior and gardens. One who did so was Joseph Aloisius Ratzinger (b 1927), who found his vocation for the priesthood confirmed here, and became Pope Benedict XVI.

voyage.name: St Ulrich
voyage.content: This may date from the 12th century. A new church was added in 1912-16, whereupon the original onion-domed church became a side-chapel. Ulrich was a 10th century Prince-Bishop in Augsburg and military leader against Magyar invasion.

voyage.name: Blutenburg Castle
voyage.content: This was built in 1438 as a hunting lodge for Albert III, Duke of Bavaria. It was on a river island between two arms of the River Würm, with the east arm dammed to create an ornamental lake - leisure rather than defence was always the intention here, and the ring wall, towers and gatehouse weren't designed against serious assault. It was embellished and extended by Albert's son Duke Sigismund, the stand-out being the

voyage.name: Hiob Monastery
voyage.content: This is Russian Orthodox. You can look in at the church and attend services.

voyage.name: DAV Kletter- und Boulderzentrum
voyage.content: Large indoor bouldering and climbing centre, gets busy out of office hours.

voyage.name: Basketball: FC Bayern Munich
voyage.content: They're better known as a soccer club, but Bayern Munich also play in Basketball Bundesliga, the game's top tier. Their home court is Rudi-Sedlmayer-Halle, sponsored as Audi Dome. It seats 6700 and was built in 1972 for the Olympics.

voyage.name: Sugar Mountain
voyage.content: Culture and activity centre in a disused concrete factory. Activities (many free) include fitness classes, bouldering, basketball and skatepark. Culture includes film, concerts, theatre, art exhibitions and warehouse raves. There's also a beer garden. In summer it hosts Kollektivgarten 3000 electro music festival.

voyage.name: Feierwerk
voyage.content: Cultural centre in a former industrial depot with live music venues (Hansa 39, Kranhalle, Orangehouse, Sunny Red), a radio station (Radio Feierwerk 92.4 ), an artist's workshop (Farbenladen) and a skatepark (Skateplatzl).

voyage.name: Sport Bittl
voyage.content: This is the main outlet of a chain of sports wear and equipment stores, specialising in mountain sports and biking. Their outlet in Laim remains closed.

voyage.name: Al Caminetto
voyage.content: Small restaurant run by two Sardinian ladies, mixed reviews for quality.

voyage.name: Mangostin
voyage.content: Excellent Thai and other Asian cuisine.

voyage.name: Asam Schlössl
voyage.content: Upscale Bavarian restaurant and beer garden in an 18th century villa.

voyage.name: Café Gans am Wasser
voyage.content: Lakeside café in Westpark which often hosts live events.

voyage.name: Augustiner Schützengarten
voyage.content: Pleasant beer hall and garden with 3000 seats serving Augustiner beer and trad food. On Sunday from 17:00 they have a live band.

voyage.name: Hopfengarten
voyage.content: This 1500 seater beer garden is next to Audi Dome (see above) in Westpark and serves Löwenbräu. It remains closed in 2022.

voyage.name: Insel Mühle
voyage.content: As the name indicates, this is a former mill on an island in the river Würm. In summer the 800-seater beer-garden serves Augustiner beer. The hotel and restaurant are open year-round.

voyage.name: Rosengarten
voyage.content: 1500-seater beer garden at the western end of the extensive Westpark (described above) serving Paulaner beer and trad food.

voyage.name: Waldwirtschaft
voyage.content: 2500-seater riverside beer garden, a pleasant bike-ride from the city. They serve Spaten beer and have a self-service buffet for trad food, and you may bring your own food to barbecue and eat at table. The music is not oompah band but jazz.

voyage.name: Zum Flaucher
voyage.content: This restaurant and beer garden is near the south end of the large Flaucher island. It has 1700 seats, serves Löwenbräu beer, and is open in summer whenever the weather is okay for sitting outside. From the U-Bahn or Bus 54 stop, access the island via the R2 bridge.

voyage.name: Nachtgalerie
voyage.content: This club is in a former railway cargo terminal. It's primarily DJ's now and seldom live music.

voyage.name: The Ape Club
voyage.content: Small techno nightclub in the very west of Munich in a former brothel with one dance floor and two chillout rooms.

voyage.name: Campingplatz Obermenzing
voyage.content: Simple campsite open March-Oct, some noise from autobahn. Normally clean but gets mobbed and squalid during Oktoberfest.

voyage.name: Camping Munich Thalkirchen
voyage.content: Peaceful bosky campsite open March-Oct on the banks of the Isar.

voyage.name: Munich Park Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Well run place open year-round, for youth hostel association members only.

voyage.name: ibis Munich City West
voyage.content: Reliable budget chain.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Munich South
voyage.content: 320-room business hotel, concrete bunker from the outside, good service inside.

voyage.name: Leonardo Hotel Munich City West
voyage.content: Efficient hotel with modern interior and a large roof terrace.

voyage.name: K+K Hotel am Harras
voyage.content: Clean comfy small hotel with good public transport.
